Adding vault storage with Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery

  • Add a storage object for vault PowerProtect DD series that is running in the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery vault environment. A vault PowerProtect DD series in the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery vault serves as the repository for the data that is replicated from the production system and protected by the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery solution.

    1. Log in to the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery UI.
    2. From the Main Menu, select Infrastructure > Assets.
    3. Click VAULT STORAGE at the top of the Assets content pane.
    4. Click Add.
    5. Complete the following fields in the dialog box:

    Figure 10.    Adding vault storage with Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery

    1. Click Save.

    The Vault Storage table lists the storage object:

    Figure 11.    Vault storage table

Conclusion

  • The Dell PowerFlex Cyber Recovery solution combines the high-performance, low-latency and easily scalable PowerFlex platform with a complete digital vault, data analysis and recovery solution through Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery and CyberSense. With the unique operational logical air gap described in this solution, organizations can be confident to have network isolation between their production and vault. By implementing this solution, PowerFlex customers can isolate and recover their critical data using the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery vault and identify suspicious activity using CyberSense.

Creating the MTree replication context

  • Steps to create the Mtree replication:

    1. Log in to the production PowerProtect DD series with the username sysadmin.
    1. Select Data Management.
    2. Select MTree.
    3. Locate the MTree where the backups are written and make a note of the MTree Name. This MTree name will be use in the Source Path field in a future step.
    4. Click Replication.
    5. Click Create Pair.
    6. Verify that the Replication Direction is set to Outbound.
    7. Verify that the Replication Type is set to MTree.
    8. Under Replication Details, the Source System should contain the FQDN for the production PowerProtect DD series.
    9. In the Source Path field, enter the MTree name entered in Step 4.
    10. Next to Destination System click Add System.
    11. The Add System window opens.
    12. In the System field, enter the FQDN for the Vault PowerProtect DD series in the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery vault.
    13. In the username field, enter the username sysadmin.
    14. In the Password field, enter the password for the user sysadmin.
    15. Click OK.
    16. In the Destination Path field, enter the same data that was entered in the Source Path field. The destination path is automatically created by the system.
    17. Click OK to create the replication pair.

    Figure 9.   Replication context in between the PowerProtect DD series

Data Analysis using CyberSense

  • Analyze a point-in-time (PIT) copy by using the CyberSense feature in the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery vault.

    For detailed information and instructions on analyzing a copy, see Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery Product Guide.

    1. Login to Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery UI and go to Policies > Copies.
    2. Select the latest copy and click Analyze. From the Application Host list box, select the application nickname for the CyberSense feature.


    Figure 19.    CyberSense as an application in Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery

    1. When the analysis is complete, return to the list of copies under Policies > Copies and click in the row of a copy. The Last Analysis column shows the results as Suspicious, Good as shown in the following figures:

    Figure 20.    Analyze the good test data operation status 

    Figure 21.    Analyze the suspicious data operation status

    The following figure shows the CyberSense output for suspicious test data found:

    Figure 22.    CyberSense GUI output for suspicious test data

    1. To retrieve a detailed analysis report (copy-name.csv) about a completed analysis, select the analyzed copy, click Analysis Report Actions, and do one of the following from the drop-down list as shown in the following figure:
      1. Click Download Analysis Report to download an analysis report for a specified copy to the location configured for download in the browser.
      2. Click Email Analysis Report to send an analysis report for a specified copy in an email message. In the drop-down list, enter at least one valid email address. You can then specify multiple email addresses. Click Apply.

    Figure 23.    Analysis report download options

Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud

  • PowerFlex software is also available in the public cloud as Dell APEX Block Storage for Public Cloud. It offers the same on-premises benefits of high-performance, linear scalability, and high resilience as in cloud. It also adds cloud-specific benefits, such as large volume sizes, extreme performance based on NVMe drives, and predictable scalability. The Dell APEX Block Storage self-healing architecture simplifies and increases the availability of infrastructure. It is designed to remain running even when it encounters failures. With fast rebuilds, Dell APEX Block Storage recovers rapidly from failures and keeps operating, without degrading performance or compromising availability. You can also extend this availability and configure it to protect your application availability across multiple availability zones.

Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery

  • Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery solution maintains mission-critical business data and technology configurations in a secure, logically air-gapped environment that secures a copy of critical data on a system that has minimal visibility to the production network, allows for forensic analysis of the protected data to detect unusual behavior that is indicative of a cyberattack, and facilitates restore in the event the environment is compromised.

    Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery Vault is isolated from all other networks with a logical air gap around the data path leading into the vault and security around the management path inside the vault.

    The solution enables periodic access to the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery Vault long enough to replicate data from the production system. At all other times, the CR Vault is secured and isolated from the network.

Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery components

  • The Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery solution includes the following components:

    Production PowerProtect DD series: The source PowerProtect DD series contains the production data that the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery solution protects.

    Vault PowerProtect DD series: The PowerProtect DD series system in the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery vault is the replication target for the source PowerProtect DD series.

    Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery software: The Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery software orchestrates data synchronization, manages, and locks the multiple data copies that are stored on the PowerProtect DD series in the Cyber Recovery vault, and orchestrates recovery.

    Backup Server: Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery offers standard recovery options to meet cyber resiliency requirements.

    CyberSense (Analytics host): Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery is the first solution with best in class (sheltered harbor) cyber data protection that is combined with an intelligent layer of protection to help find data corruption when an attack penetrates the data center. CyberSense is deployed on the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery Vault environment. It uses machine learning (ML) to analyze the backup copies in the vault with over 100 content-based statistics and detects signs of corruption due to ransomware. CyberSense detects corruption with up to 99.5 percent confidence, identifies threats, and diagnoses attack vectors while protecting the business-critical content –all within the security of the vault.

    Note: Contact the Backup and Recovery Design Center for validating and properly sizing the Cyber Recovery solution.

    1. Log in to Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery UI and go to Policies tab.
    2. Click Add to add a new policy, The user interface displays the available policy types: Standard and PowerProtect Data Manager.

               Figure 14. Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery policy types

    1. For backup software other than PowerProtect Data Manager, select the Policy Type as Standard.
    2. Select the storage object containing the replication context that the policy protects.
    3. Under Context, select the MTree replication context to protect and the interface on the storage instance that is configured for replications.
    4. Under Ethernet Port, select the interface on the storage instance that is configured for replications.

    Note: Do not select the data or management Ethernet interfaces.

    Use the following steps to run the policy immediately:

    1. Log in to Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery UI.Select Policies in the Main menu.
    1. On the Policies content pane, select the policy checkbox. Then click Actions and select the following actions that you want the policy to perform. Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery runs the policy and displays progress messages on the Jobs content pane and the dashboard.

    Figure 15.    Actions available for policy

    1. Secure Copy: Sync the data, create a fast copy, put Retention Lock on the copy.
    2. Sync Copy: Sync the data and create a fast copy.
    3. Sync: Sync the data.
    4. Copy: Create a fast copy of data that is already on PowerProtect DD series in the vault environment.
    5. Copy Lock: Put the Retention Lock on a copy or extend the lock duration.

Deploying Dell PowerProtect DD Series in a Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery Vault environment

  • Use the following steps to deploy vault PowerProtect DD series in the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery Vault environment.

    • Configure the replication with the procedures provided in the following sections.
    • Ensure that the PowerProtect DD file system is created and is enabled.

Executive summary

  • Global businesses rely on the constant flow of data across interconnected networks, and digital transformation leads to an increase of sensitive data transfer. This increased data flow increases the opportunity for cyber threats and exposure of data for ransom, corporate espionage, or even cyber warfare.

    The PowerFlex family offers key value propositions for traditional and cloud-native production workloads, deployment flexibility, linear scalability, predictable high performance, and enterprise-grade resilience.

    Dell PowerProtect Data Manager enables users to protect, manage, and recover data in on-premises, virtual, or cloud deployments. The PowerProtect Data Manager platform provides centralized governance that helps mitigate risk and assures compliance of SLAs and SLOs through protection workflows. The PowerProtect Data Manager enhances protection by sending data directly to the Dell PowerProtect DD series to gain benefits from high efficiency, deduplication, performance, and scalability.

    Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery protects business-critical data and minimizes the impact of a cyberattack.

    This whitepaper describes how mission-critical business data and technology configurations for PowerFlex on-premises deployments can be stored in a secure, logically air-gapped environment. This secure copy allows for forensic analysis of the protected data to uncover unusual behavior that is indicative of a cyberattack. This protection includes file corruption, encryption of files or pages in a database, or deletions and creations. Also, a secure copy of critical data has no access from the production network.

Independent architecture

  • In an independent architecture, or two-layer architecture, some nodes provide storage capacity and host datasets while other, separate, and independent nodes, host applications and workloads. Compute and storage resources can be scaled independently by adding nodes to the cluster. This separation of compute and storage resources can also help minimize software licensing costs in certain situations. And this architecture can be ideal for hosting high-performance high-value databases and application workloads.

Installation steps

  • Steps to install the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery software:

    1. From the vSphere Client in the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery Vault, use the Deploy OVF Template wizard to deploy the PowerProtect Cyber Recovery virtual appliance file.
    2. When the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery virtual appliance deployment is completed, open the vCenter console for the newly deployed appliance.
    3. Log in as the root user using the default password changeme.
    1. Run the following command to begin the installation.

    # crsetup.sh –deploy

       5. At the prompts, enter a unique passphrase or password for the Cyber Recovery Security Officer (crso), the Cyber Recovery lockbox, and MongoDB. The installation procedure starts Cyber Recovery services.

    Note: Remember the lockbox passphrase. It is required to perform upgrades and reset the Security Officers password. If you forget the lockbox passphrase, you must reinstall the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery software. 

    1. Log out of the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery software and then do the following:
      1. Use SSH to access the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery virtual    appliance as the admin user with the password changeme.
      2. Change the password.
      3. Use the su command to switch to root.
      4. Enter the root password changeme.
      5. At the prompt, change the password.
      6. Log out of the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery software and then do the following:
      7. Use SSH to access the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery virtual appliance as the admin user with the password changeme.
      8. Change the password.
      9. Use the su command to switch to root.
      10. Enter the root password changeme.
      11. At the prompt, change the password.
    2. Go to the URL shown at the end of the installation script. Then, log in to the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery UI using the default Security Officer (crso) account and the password that you created.

Home > Storage > PowerFlex > White Papers > Ransomware Protection: Secure Your Data on Dell PowerFlex with PowerProtect Cyber Recovery > Logical air gap

Logical air gap

  • The term air gap implies physical isolation from an unsecure system or network. A logical air gap describes a physical connection but logical isolation from the network. The logical air gap provides another layer of defense by reducing the solutions overall attack surface.

    Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery provides a logical air gap feature to keep the PowerProtect Cyber Recovery Vault disconnected from the production network. The PowerProtect Cyber Recovery Vault is disconnected from the production network and is only connected when Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery triggers replication through short, policy-driven intervals. A preconfigured port in the vault firewall is enabled only for data ingestion and is disabled once the replication is completed. This configuration ensures that the Cyber Recovery Vault is isolated from the production network.

    Figure 7.   Logical air gap in Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery vault

    The vault PowerProtect DD series in the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery Vault limits communication to the production PowerProtect DD series during the data synchronization operation.

Logical architecture

  • The following diagram shows a logical architecture that is deployed on a two-layer PowerFlex cluster setup with four storage-only nodes and four compute-only nodes.

     

    Figure 5.   Logical architecture of Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery

    Production environment: The production environment is deployed on a two-layer PowerFlex cluster containing storage-only nodes that are deployed on the embedded operating system, running the SDS component and compute-only nodes deployed on VMware hypervisor, running the SDC component.

    For more information about the configuration of PowerFlex nodes, see Configuration details.

    The production data of the customer is protected and managed by Dell PowerProtect Data Manager which stores the backup data on the production PowerProtect DD series appliance. In a Dell PowerProtect CR solution, the production PowerProtect DD series replicates the data to a PowerProtect DD series appliance in the CR Vault.

    Vault environment: The Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery Vault environment contains a PowerProtect DD series appliance and the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery management host that runs the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery software. Data from the production environment enters the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery Vault environment through PowerProtect DD series MTree replication.

    The infrastructure in the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery vault is deployed on a VMware ESXi cluster.

    Additional safeguards include an automated operational logical air gap to provide network isolation from the production network.

MTree replication

Dell.com Contact Us
Share
United States/English

Home > Storage > PowerFlex > White Papers > Ransomware Protection: Secure Your Data on Dell PowerFlex with PowerProtect Cyber Recovery > MTree replication

MTree replication

  • MTree replication is a PowerProtect DD series feature that enables copying unique data from the production PowerProtect DD series MTree to the PowerProtect DD series MTree in the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery vault.

    MTree replication synchronizes data between the production environment and the logically air-gapped Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery Vault. There are three levels of compliance:

    •  None
    • Governance (not immutable)
    • Compliance. Compliance is the only option that supports retention lock and creates immutable copies on the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery vault. The copies can be used for recovery and analytics after being copied to a read/write PowerProtect DD series MTree.

    The Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery software controls data synchronization from the production environment to the vault environment by PowerProtect DD series MTree replication. After the datasets and associated MTrees to be protected by the Dell PowerProtect Cyber Recovery solution are determined, replication contexts are set up between the production and vault PowerProtect DD series.

    MTree replication is designed so that all data within an MTree is replicated securely between the production and vault PowerProtect DD series. After initial synchronization is completed and all data is copied to the vault PowerProtect DD series, each subsequent synchronization operation only copies data segments that are new or have been updated.

PowerFlex CSI/CSM 

  • An important component outside of PowerFlex that enables a flexible consumption model for Kubernetes is the PowerFlex CSI driver, developed as a part of the Dell Kubernetes strategy. After loading the CSI driver for PowerFlex into Kubernetes, it can be used to provision persistent volumes from the underlying PowerFlex storage resource. If the Kubernetes deployment is running low on PowerFlex storage resources, you can add PowerFlex storage nodes to increase the system capacity and performance.  

     The CSI driver connects the PowerFlex system and Kubernetes deployments. It is a storage broker which dynamically provisions volumes from PowerFlex through the PowerFlex API gateway to the Kubernetes cluster. Once the volume is available on PowerFlex, it is immediately mapped to the requesting pod. If a pod is destroyed or rescheduled, the CSI plug-in ensures that the volumes are remapped upon rescheduling of that pod.   

    • Customers running Kubernetes clusters on PowerFlex use the Dell Container Storage Modules (CSM), which extend the CSI driver capabilities. These modules:  
    • Provide enterprise storage capabilities to Kubernetes for cloud-native stateful applications.   
    • Reduce management complexity, so that developers can independently use enterprise storage with ease and automate daily operations.   
    • Extends storage functionality and capabilities beyond using the CSI driver alone. 

    These modules include snapshot, observability, authorization, application mobility, and resiliency.   

    Figure 4.   PowerFlex for different Kubernetes distributions 

    PowerFlex supports multiple operating systems, different deployment options on-premises and public cloud deployment model. PowerFlex is validated with the leading Kubernetes distributions as shown in Figure 4.

PowerFlex with NVMe over TCP (NVMe/TCP)

  • NVMe is a family of open specifications that defines an industry standard for both a logical interface and a communication protocol for accessing block storage across an internal PCIe fabric or through external fabrics such as TCP/IP and FC. NVMe is designed to take advantage of the internal parallelism and low latency inherent in flash-based media SSDs. 

    NVMe/TCP is an extension of the NVMe base specification that defines the binding of the NVMe protocol to message-based fabrics using TCP. By binding the NVMe protocol to TCP, NVMe/TCP enables the efficient end-to-end transfer of commands and data between NVMe hosts and NVMe controller devices by any standard Ethernet-based TCP/IP networks. 

    From PowerFlex release 4.x onwards, support for NVMe/TCP has been added for on-premises deployment with the introduction of a new Storage Data Target (SDT) component that is installed in the storage layer. The NVMe initiator in the operating system or hypervisor communicates with the SDT, which then communicates with the Storage Data Server (SDS). The NVMe initiator is part of the kernel of the application host operating system or hypervisor.   

    Figure 2.  PowerFlex with NVMe/TCP

    For more information, see PowerFlex with NVMe over TCP.

Scheduling Policies

  • Schedules are created for each policy which run the specified action at scheduled intervals.

    1. Log in to the Dell PowerProtect Cyber recovery UI.
    2. Select Policies from the Main Menu.
    3. Click Schedules at the top of the Policies content pane.
    4. Click Add and enter the following fields:
      1. Schedule Name: Name of the schedule.
      2. Policy: Policy which is go to schedule.
      3. Action: Actions that the policy performs.
      4. Retention Lock Duration: Only selected Secure Copy or Copy Lock as the action, enter the duration of the retention lock that this policy applies to PIT copies.
      5. Application Host: Only when selected Analyze as the action, select the host for CyberSense feature.
      6. Frequency: The frequency in days and hours.
      7. Next Run Date: The date to start running the policy under this schedule.
      8. Next Run Time: The time to start running the policy under this schedule.
    1. Click Apply. The Schedules table lists the schedules.

Securing copies

  • The policies page can be used to view and secure copies.

    Steps to secure a copy:

    1. Select Policies from the Main Menu.
    2. On the Policies content pane, click Copies to display the list of existing copies.
    3. Select the copy that you want to secure and click Lock.
    4. In the Lock dialog box, specify the retention period and click Save. 
    5. The retention lock is set. The Expiration Date column changes from No lock set and displays the expiration date and a locked icon. When the retention lock expires, the Expiration Date column displays the expiration date and an unlocked icon.
